$comment: Golden corpus: reviewed expectations for what validates, independent of any one implementation.
currentVerdict is what the live hand-written Zod schemas do NOW. It is asserted on every run,
which is what makes Tier B a differential oracle rather than a record of history.
v1Verdict is the reviewed target contract, asserted against the derived validator once it exists.
A row may omit v1Verdict while a divergence is still an unreviewed candidate.
Resolved divergences keep their history in `regression`, which is documentation and never asserted.
Rows are added when a decision is made, not scraped from current behaviour, so the file records
contract rather than whatever the schemas happened to do.

rows.description: A container with required wrappers and a child field
rows.rationale: ContainerField reconciliation gate. Runtime support was proven across all four adapters before the schema changed, so accepting it is an evidence-backed contract expansion rather than an inference from the type registry.

regression.issue: ContainerField was registered in FieldRegistryContainers and rendered by core BUILT_IN_FIELDS, but validation rejected it as an unknown field type

rows.description: A container with no wrappers property
rows.rationale: `wrappers` is required on ContainerField. A container without it is a group spelled differently, so accepting it would erase the distinction that justifies the type. This row exists to stop a future derivation from relaxing the property to optional.

rows.description: A page cannot declare container-level validators
rows.rationale: Pages flatten into the form and have no schema path of their own, so container-level validation has no value to run against. Use a group or array for cross-field validation.

regression.issue: Moving container validation properties out of the shared forbidden list caused pages to accept validators that Zod then stripped

rows.description: A container cannot contain a page
rows.rationale: ContainerAllowedChildren excludes pages because pages are top-level navigation boundaries. The runtime validator and MCP guidance must enforce the same placement rule.

regression.issue: The newly accepted container schema used the unrestricted recursive field schema without a matching pre-validation nesting rule

rows.description: An add-array-item button with nothing to add
rows.rationale: `template` says what the button adds, and the type has always declared it required. A button with no template renders a control that cannot do anything, so accepting it hands an agent a form that looks finished and is not. Tightening this rejects JSON configs that passed before, which is why the decision belongs in the corpus rather than only in a schema.

regression.issue: add, prepend and insert array-item buttons validated with no template, so the schema accepted a button with nothing to insert while TypeScript rejected the same config

rows.description: A remove-array-item button, which needs no template
rows.rationale: The bound on the row above. Requiring `template` on the buttons that insert must not spread to the ones that do not: a remove button has nothing to build, and demanding a template from it would reject correct config to enforce a rule that does not apply to it.

rows.description: A select whose options sit on the field
rows.rationale: Placement is the pitfall agents hit most often, and it is the payoff the derivation claims: SelectField declares `options` while SelectProps is empty, so field level is the only correct spelling. Pinned here so a derivation that started reading props as the home for options fails instead of quietly accepting both.

rows.description: A select whose options were put inside props
rows.rationale: The mirror of the row above, and the reason it is worth asserting: a schema that accepted both placements would teach the mistake rather than catch it, and the field would silently render with no options at runtime.

Rows nest at runtime, which is how a twelve-column grid is subdivided. Validation used to reject it, so a layout that rendered correctly could not be written down. Accepting it follows the runtime rather than the other way round.

regression.issue: a row listed as an allowed child of a row in the type registry was rejected by validation, so nested grid layouts that rendered correctly could not pass the CLI

rows.description: A row holding a hidden field
rows.rationale: A hidden field carries a value and occupies no space, so forbidding it inside a row forced authors to hoist it out of the group it belongs to and lose that association for no layout benefit.

rows.description: A container nested inside a container
rows.rationale: The bound on the row above. Containers are layout primitives that flatten into the parent, and the type lists `ContainerField` among its own allowed children, so forbidding `page` must not spill into forbidding the nesting the type permits.
